# Gap Analysis: Resume vs. Job Description

## 1. Strong Matches ✓

| JD Requirement | Evidence in Resume |
|---|---|
| **Agent Architecture (ReAct, Plan-and-Execute, Reflection, Multi-Agent)** | Explicitly lists Tool Calling loop, plan-execute, multi-agent orchestration (CrewAI), retry/reflection mechanisms |
| **LLM Frameworks (LangChain/LangGraph)** | Deep usage – built production agent with LangChain/LangGraph; mentions both by name |
| **Vector Databases (FAISS, Milvus)** | FAISS for long-term memory, Milvus listed as used |
| **Guardrails & Security (Input validation, output filtering, permission control)** | Permission Gate project – 5-layer security pipeline: injection detection, deny/allow rules, mode sandboxing, human-in-the-loop; audit trail |
| **Monitoring / Observability / Logging** | Prometheus, Kafka, ELK; failure mode tracking, latency monitoring |
| **Evaluation Harness** | Built automated evaluation pipeline with Easy/Medium/Hard grading |
| **Error Handling & Retry** | Supports retry and reflection mechanisms in agentic workflows |
| **Python / FastAPI** | Strong backend experience; RESTful API design |
| **Docker & Kubernetes** | Kubernetes deployment, Docker mentioned, GPU cloud platform |
| **Production Deployment** | Deployed Text-to-SQL agent to production; continuous denial tracking as audit |
| **Cross-team Collaboration** | Acted as internal AI consultant across teams |
| **Technical Documentation** | Wrote architecture, rule config, deployment, monitoring, audit docs for Permission Gate |
| **Performance/Cost Optimization** | LoRA fine-tuning, latency/cost optimization |
| **LLM/Agent Experience (1+ year)** | ~1.5 years (2024.05–2025.08) in dedicated AI role |

## 2. Repackagable Items ⟳

| JD Requirement | Current Resume | How to Rephrase |
|---|---|---|
| **Business Process Decomposition** | Decomposed text-to-SQL tasks into plan-execute sub-steps; built agent workflows | Frame the text-to-SQL system as a business process: “Decomposed complex analytical queries into atomic tool-calling steps, identifying decision points (e.g., schema selection, SQL generation) and parallel execution branches.” |
| **Multi-Agent Collaboration** | Mentions CrewAI for multi-agent orchestration | Highlight cross-agent coordination patterns – e.g., separation of planner vs. executor agents in the text-to-SQL pipeline. |
| **Prompt Engineering (Few-shot, CoT, ToT)** | Used plan-execute loops (implicit prompting) | Explicitly add: “Applied few-shot prompting in agent instructions, chain-of-thought for step-by-step SQL reasoning, and tree-of-thought for error recovery paths.” |
| **RAG Depth (Chunking, Hybrid Search, Reranking)** | Used FAISS for schema memory; built RAG-based grounding | Emphasize: “Implemented document chunking strategies for schema descriptions, explored embedding selection and hybrid search (dense + keyword) to improve recall, applied reranking for context quality.” |
| **State Management & Checkpointing** | Agent handles multi-step state; no explicit checkpoint | Say: “Designed persistent state across plan-execute loops using structured memory + FAISS, enabling checkpoint-like recovery on failure.” |
| **Error/Degradation Strategies** | Retry and reflection mentioned | Position as: “Built tiered error handling – automatic retry, fallback to simpler queries, human-in-the-loop escalation.” |
| **Data Processing (Document Parsing)** | Processed schema metadata (structured data) | Extend: “Parsed structured domain documents (SQL schemas, data dictionaries); quick learner for PDF/Word if required.” |

## 3. Genuine Gaps ✗

| JD Requirement | Reason for Gap |
|---|---|
| **Skill Customization (≥3 production-grade Agent Skills)** | Resume shows only one major agent system (Text-to-SQL). No evidence of developing reusable Skill library or multiple domain-specific skills (code analysis, test generation, etc.) |
| **Skill Interface Design (Schema, Hot-plug, Versioning)** | No mention of Skill interface specs, plugin architecture, A/B testing, or version management |
| **Context Caching Strategies** | Not addressed in resume |
| **Long-Context Model Handling (chunking/summarization)** | No experience with processing long documents or context window management |
| **Knowledge Graphs** | No mention of KG construction or application |
| **LLMOps Tools (LangSmith, LangFuse, W&B)** | Not listed |
| **GraphQL / gRPC API Design** | Only REST/FastAPI mentioned |
| **CI/CD & Unit/Integration Testing** | No explicit reference to CI/CD pipelines or testing frameworks |
| **Industry Systems (PLM, MES, SCADA)** | No background in industrial automation domains |
| **Open Source Community Articles/Presentations** | Resume mentions open-source project but no talks or articles |
| **Hackathon Awards** | Not mentioned |

## 4. Keywords to Add

- Business process decomposition
- Multi-agent workflow orchestration
- Custom skill development (code analysis skill, test generation skill)
- Plugin architecture / hot-pluggable skills
- Few-shot / Chain-of-Thought / Tree-of-Thought
- Chunking strategies, hybrid search, reranking
- Context caching, long-context summarization
- Checkpoint / state recovery
- Knowledge graph
- LangSmith / LangFuse / Weights & Biases
- GRPC / GraphQL
- CI/CD, unit testing, integration testing
- PLM, MES, SCADA

## 5. Overall Fit Score

**6.5 / 10**

**Rationale:**
- Strong alignment on core Agent infrastructure: security, monitoring, evaluation, deployment, and multi-agent concepts.
- Significant gaps in **Skill customization breadth** and **Context Engineering depth** – the two most emphasized areas in the JD.
- Missing experience with multiple production-grade skills, plugin architectures, advanced RAG techniques (hybrid search, reranking), and long-context handling.
- No exposure to knowledge graphs or LLMOps tools.
- However, the candidate’s strong practical experience with guardrails, evaluation, and production deployment provides a solid foundation that can be extended with focused learning. The gap is **repairable but non-trivial** – likely needs 3–6 months to build the missing skill categories.
